title: Can Foreigners Buy Property in Romania? EU vs Non-EU Rules Explained
metaDescription: Foreign ownership of Romanian real estate explained: what EU citizens can buy, the restrictions on non-EU buyers, the company route for land, and how the process works remotely.
h1: Foreigners Buying Property in Romania: What the Rules Actually Say
whatsappPrefillEn: Hello! I am a foreign buyer interested in Romanian property and need help with verification and registration.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.html:
Romania distinguishes between buildings and land, and between EU/EEA citizens and everyone else:

  • Buildings (apartments, houses): any foreigner, from anywhere, can own them. The building's ownership is straightforward — note only that a house normally comes with its land, which is where the land rules enter.
  • Land — EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and companies: may acquire land in Romania essentially on the same footing as Romanians, a right settled since the post-accession transition periods expired (2012 for most land, 2014 for agricultural and forest land).
  • Land — non-EU citizens: may only acquire land directly under international-treaty reciprocity conditions, which in practice rarely helps. The standard, entirely lawful route: a Romanian company — even one wholly owned by the foreign investor — is a Romanian legal person and can own land without restriction. Most non-EU investment in Romanian land is structured this way; inheritance by law is the other main exception, as inherited land can be owned by non-EU heirs.

One more layer applies to everyone, foreigners and Romanians alike: extravilan agricultural land carries the pre-emption procedure of Law 17/2014 — sellers must first offer the land to a ranked list of preferred buyers. It is a process, not a prohibition; see the dedicated guide.

This page is practical orientation, not legal advice — structure and citizenship questions belong with a Romanian lawyer, and rules evolve. What follows is the part that does not change: whatever entity buys, the land itself must check out.

sections.heading: The real risk is rarely the citizenship rule
sections.html:
In our experience, foreign buyers stopped by the ownership rules are rare; foreign buyers burned by unverified land are not. The dangers are the same ones facing any buyer — unregistered parcels, co-ownership tangles, area discrepancies, overlaps, encumbrances — amplified by distance, language and unfamiliarity with the land book system. The cure is also the same: a fresh land registry extract read by someone who knows what Part III means, and a due diligence survey confirming the ground matches the paper, before money becomes non-refundable.

Everything transactional works remotely: powers of attorney (notarized and apostilled in your country, or signed at a Romanian consulate), your Romanian lawyer at the deed, and our verification and registration reports arriving on WhatsApp in English. Many of our foreign clients have never visited the land they safely own.

items.q: I'm a UK/US/Swiss citizen. Can I buy a house with a garden?
items.a: Swiss citizens are treated with EU-equivalent rights for these purposes. UK citizens lost EU status after Brexit, and US citizens never had it — for them, directly acquiring the land under the house runs into the non-EU restriction, and the practical routes are the Romanian company structure or rights like superficie; buildings themselves are unrestricted. Exact structuring is lawyer territory — we handle the property verification whichever route you take.

items.q: Does buying property give me residency?
items.a: No — Romania has no golden-visa scheme tied to property purchase. Residency runs through separate immigration rules; ownership and residency are independent questions.

items.q: Is the Romanian-company route legitimate or a loophole?
items.a: Fully legitimate and expressly how the system works: a Romanian-registered company is a Romanian legal person regardless of who owns its shares. Thousands of foreign-owned companies own Romanian land, farms and project sites this way. Your lawyer sets it up; the land the company buys still deserves the same technical diligence.

items.q: Can a foreigner inherit Romanian land?
items.a: Yes — legal inheritance is the classic exception through which non-EU citizens lawfully own Romanian land. Registering inherited land, often unregistered and shared among heirs, is exactly the kind of work we do daily.
